questions.prompt: Which is NOT one of the three things a load balancer gives you?
options: Faster individual requests on each backend
Clients know one stable address, so you can deploy, resize, and replace servers behind it

questions.prompt: Routing each user back to the same server every time is called ______ sessions. (one word)
Load balancing works most cleanly when backends are stateless and the state lives in a database or cache.
What does "cattle, not pets" mean for servers?
options: Servers should be named after animals
Servers are interchangeable and can be replaced without care
Each server is hand-tuned and irreplaceable

questions.prompt: A server keeps login sessions in its own memory and crashes. What happens to its users?
options: Nothing: another server has the sessions
They lose their sessions and must log in again
They're moved with their sessions intact
